passage:
Omkar,
I owe you an apology, a proper one, not a quick "sorry" in the corridor.
When the class trip money went missing from the monitor's desk, I told Ma'am I was sure it was you. You wouldn't look at anyone, you kept tapping your pen, and your voice went shaky. I thought that was proof.
Yesterday the money turned up in the sports-room register, where the monitor had left it. Nobody took it.
My cousin, who studies psychology, told me that nervous people telling the truth can look exactly like that, and people who lie can look perfectly calm. I didn't know that. You were probably nervous because I was staring at you.
I'm sorry I made the whole class look at you that way. I'll tell Ma'am too.
Kiran

qa.q: Where did the trip money turn up?
qa.a: In the sports-room register, where the monitor had left it.

qa.q: Why was Kiran so sure Omkar had taken the money?
qa.a: Kiran believed that not looking at anyone, tapping a pen and a shaky voice were proof of lying.

qa.q: What could Kiran do differently the next time something goes missing?
qa.a: Kiran could check the facts first, such as where the money was last kept, instead of reading guilt from nervousness.

qa.q: What was it like for Omkar to be suspected in front of the class?
qa.a: Omkar was probably frightened and humiliated, and being stared at likely made the nervousness even stronger.

grounding: A teenager who took fidgeting and avoided eye contact as proof of lying learns such cues are weak, since nervous truth-tellers look the same.

passage:
What did I learn in Class 11? That I'm terrible at spotting liars. I'm Baljeet, and so is everyone, probably.
During the student council election, someone ran an anonymous page mocking the candidates. Everyone suspected a quiet boy from 11C, because when the teacher questioned him he stammered, went red and stared at his shoes. I was sure too.
Then my friend Bidisha looked me straight in the eye and said, "It's horrible. I'd never do that." Totally calm. I believed her completely.
Two weeks later the school found the page had been made from her account.
So now when someone says "you can tell by their eyes", I think of that boy's red face and Bidisha's steady one. I check facts now, not faces.

qa.q: What did Bidisha say when asked about the page?
Why did Baljeet believe Bidisha so completely?
qa.a: Bidisha looked Baljeet straight in the eye and stayed totally calm, which Baljeet took as a sign of honesty.

qa.q: What does Baljeet do now instead of reading faces?
qa.a: Baljeet checks facts, not faces, since both the steady eyes and the red cheeks turned out to be misleading.

qa.q: How might the quiet boy from 11C have felt while everyone suspected him?
qa.a: He likely felt scared and ashamed, which made him stammer and go red even though he had done nothing.

grounding: A teenager learns that a calm, eye-contact denial and a stammering, red-faced one say little about who is honest.
